package_info.why_malicious: The injected code is designed to steal payment card data from e-commerce customers by intercepting and exfiltrating sensitive information during the checkout process. The code is loaded from an external, attacker-controlled domain and operates without user consent, violating the integrity and security of the affected websites.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (checkout page load and form submission)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into Magento 1 checkout page templates (e.g., app/design/frontend/base/default/template/checkout/onepage.phtml or similar)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code loads a remote JavaScript file from naturalfreshmall.com, which executes in the context of the checkout page, intercepts payment form data, and exfiltrates it to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading JavaScript from an unrelated, external domain on a payment page is highly suspicious, especially when the domain is not associated with the e-commerce site.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout pages should only load scripts from trusted, first-party or vetted third-party sources. Injecting scripts from unknown domains is not expected.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate analytics or payment providers load scripts from external domains, but these are well-known and documented.
key_indicators: Script injected into sensitive payment workflow
No legitimate business reason for this external script

execution_context.file_location: Loaded from https://naturalfreshmall.com/xxx.js, executed in browser

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks the checkout form submission, collects payment card details from the DOM, and sends them via HTTPS POST to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment card data to an external server is a classic sign of a payment skimmer.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Payment data should only be sent to the legitimate payment processor, not to third-party or unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may collect card data, but only to their own secure endpoints and with user consent.
key_indicators: Direct access to payment card fields
Exfiltration of sensitive data to external domain

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to Magento 1 store via SQL injection or PHP object injection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify website files and inject malicious code.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script tag is injected into checkout page templates to load external JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-controlled JavaScript in customer browsers.

attack_chain.action: External JavaScript hooks into the checkout form, collects payment card data, and exfiltrates it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of customer payment information (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Checkout page loading JavaScript from untrusted or newly registered domains
JavaScript code accessing payment form fields and sending data to external servers
Unexpected modification of checkout page templates
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS requests to naturalfreshmall.com or similar domains from customer browsers during checkout
POST requests containing payment card data to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized script tags referencing external domains in checkout page templates, inspect network traffic from checkout pages for exfiltration of payment data, and audit file integrity of Magento template files for unexpected modifications.
